family.invariant_demand: Use one declared axis system, preserve signed directional information, combine corresponding vector components, impose any stated resultant-component constraint, preserve subtraction order, and resolve a magnitude-and-angle vector by explicit projection geometry when components are not already given.
family.difficult_move: Keeping the requested direction attached to the correct signed component equation and identifying the angle reference before assigning sine/cosine, rather than using magnitude arithmetic or story-specific shortcuts.
family.independent_check: Use an alternate representation: rough arrow geometry must agree with component signs; a constrained component must satisfy its target; swapping subtraction operands must negate the result; resolved components must reconstruct the original magnitude.

support_ladder.handed_over: The axis directions, relevant component equation, and requested vector operation are supplied.
The axis directions and requested resultant condition are supplied.
Only the physical/geometric description and requested resultant are supplied.

transfer.changed_demand: Two vectors are described by a diagram or words and must first be written as signed components before they can be added.
A requested direction must be translated into a target value for one resultant component before solving for an unknown input contribution.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: which component is constrained and what target value it must take

transfer.changed_demand: The same pair of vectors is presented in the opposite subtraction order.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: the final orientation of the difference

transfer.changed_demand: A vector is given only by magnitude, quadrant and an acute angle to one axis, so signed x/y components must be constructed before vector or kinematics equations can be used.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: which component is adjacent/opposite to the stated angle and what signs the axes require
